title: “Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted…
content: “Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … with feeling … with perception … with formations … with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, knowledge arises: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not…
content:
“Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Would that man drink from that bronze cup if he knew: ‘If I drink from this, I will meet death or deadly suffering’?”
“No, venerable sir.”
“So too, Sunakkhatta, a monk should surely guard himself in regard to the six sense-bases. Knowing that ‘Attachment is the root of suffering,’ he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. It does not happen that he would still focus his body on attachment or direct his mind to attachment.”

title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
content: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

title: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?”…
content: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?” - “The sign of the beautiful.” For one who attends unwisely to the sign of the beautiful, unarisen greed arises and arisen greed increases and grows. This, good sirs, is the cause, this is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed and for the growth and increase of arisen greed.

title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior…
content: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior fights with noble warrior, brahmin fights with brahmin, householder fights with householder, mother fights with child, child fights with mother, father fights with child, child fights with father, brother fights with brother, brother fights with sister, sister fights with brother, friend fights with friend. Having engaged in quarrels, disputes, and battles, they attack one another with fists, with stones, with sticks, with swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
content: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of greed, monks, these six things should be developed.”

title: “What leads the world along? What torments itself? And what is the one thing Upon which everything depends?” “Craving leads the world along, Craving torments…
content:
“What leads the world along?
What torments itself?
And what is the one thing
Upon which everything depends?”

“Craving leads the world along,
Craving torments itself,
Craving is the one thing
Upon which everything depends.”

title: “Householder, the form element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the form element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ The…
content: “Householder, the form element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the form element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ The feeling element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the feeling element … The perception element … The formation element … The consciousness element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the consciousness element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ Thus, householder, is wandering with a home.”

title: Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality, Insult, injury, bondage, That one stands firm, Like a mountain unshaken — Such a monk, Pleasure and pain…
content:
Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality,
Insult, injury, bondage,
That one stands firm,
Like a mountain unshaken —
Such a monk,
Pleasure and pain do not disturb.

title: “Monks, there are these three elements of escape. What three? The escape from sensual pleasures — that is renunciation. The escape from form — that…
content:
“Monks, there are these three elements of escape. What three? The escape from sensual pleasures — that is renunciation. The escape from form — that is the formless. And as to whatever has come to be, is conditioned, dependently arisen, its escape is its cessation. These, monks, are the three elements of escape.

Knowing the escape from sensual pleasures,
And transcending all forms,
Always ardent, calming all conditioned things —
That monk sees rightly.

From that, being thus liberated,
He perfects direct knowledge,
Dwells at peace, in that very life,
That sage has crossed beyond all yokes.”
